'''Joseph Graham''' (born June 11, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He holds the [[NBA draft combine]] bench press record.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Merritt |first=Greg |date=November 2, 2023 |title=10 Strongest NBA Players Ever |url=https://thebarbell.com/strongest-nba-players/}}</ref>

==College career==
Graham played college basketball for the [[UCF Knights men's basketball|University of Central Florida]] (2000–02) and [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State University]] (2003–05). He averaged 13.0 points and 5.2 rebounds in four collegiate seasons and helped OSU to the Final Four in his junior campaign.<ref name=insidehoops>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/graham-option-102907.shtml|title=Raptors exercise 4th year option on Joey Graham|work=insidehoops.com|date=October 29, 2007|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Toronto Raptors (2005–2009)===
Graham was selected by the [[Toronto Raptors]] with the 16th overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]].<ref name="insidehoops" /> In his first two seasons with the Raptors, he averaged 6.5 points and 3.1 rebounds in 159 regular season games, and shot .826 (218–264) from the charity stripe. He registered a career-high 19 points on five occasions and grabbed a personal-best 12 rebounds on March 30, 2007, against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref name="insidehoops" />

Graham missed the majority of Toronto's November schedule in the 2007–08 season. He appeared in a career-low 38 games in 2007–08.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/grahajo01/gamelog/2008/|title=Joey Graham 2007–08 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref> He averaged career highs in 2008–09, with 7.7 points and 3.7 rebounds per game. On February 1, 2009, he recorded a career-high-tying 12 rebounds against the [[Orlando Magic]]. Three days later, he scored a career-high 24 points against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Another six days later, he tied his career high with 24 points against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.nba.com/player/101121/career/|title=Joey Graham|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets and Cleveland Cavaliers (2009–2011)===
[[File:Cavs Defense.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Graham (#12) with the Cavaliers in January 2011]]
On September 26, 2009, Graham signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4505982|title=Nuggets sign forward Graham|work=ESPN.com|date=September 26, 2009|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref> On July 30, 2010, Graham signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/graham_100730.html|title=Cavs Sign Joey Graham|work=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2010|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref> On December 9, 2011, prior to the start of the 2011–12 training camp period, Graham was waived by the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/training_camp_111209.html|title=Cavaliers Announce 2011–12 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2011|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref>

===D-League and Puerto Rico (2012–2013)===
On March 19, 2012, Graham was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://origin.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_acquire_joey_graham_2012_03_19.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20171226101559/http://origin.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_acquire_joey_graham_2012_03_19.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 26, 2017|title=BayHawks Acquire Joey Graham|work=NBA.com|date=March 19, 2012|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref>

On May 4, 2012, Graham signed with [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/america/other-leagues/91698/mets-de-guaynabo-land-joey-graham.html|title=Mets de Guaynabo land Joey Graham|work=Sportando.com|date=May 4, 2012|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref>

In February 2013, Graham joined [[Capitanes de Arecibo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elaybenditopr.wordpress.com/2013/03/05/capitanes-de-puerto-rico-lda2013/|title=Capitanes de Puerto Rico LDA2013|work=elaybenditopr.wordpress.com|date=March 5, 2013|access-date=December 26, 2017|language=es}}</ref> On April 15, 2013, he parted ways with Arecibo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/america/other-leagues/100532/joey-graham-and-stephen-graham-part-ways-with-capitanes-de-arecibo.html|title=Joey Graham and Stephen Graham part ways with Capitanes de Arecibo|work=Sportando.com|date=April 15, 2013|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref> Two days later, he signed with Mets de Guaynabo, returning to the team for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/america/other-leagues/100579/joey-graham-signs-with-mets-de-guaynabo.html|title=Joey Graham signs with Mets de Guaynabo|work=Sportando.com|date=April 17, 2013|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref>

==Personal==
Graham's twin brother, [[Stephen Graham (basketball)|Stephen]], also played in the NBA. His father, Joe Graham, is a former Navy airman.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/features/graham_flying_20100311.html|title=NBA twin brothers are literal high-fliers|work=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2010|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref>
